marta: Heads-up — customer corp_zephyr opened a P1: embeddings API returning 400 'dimension mismatch' when they try to index vectors. They say they send 1536-d floats but the model responds expecting 1024. Repro steps from them below.

marta: Repro (from customer):
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer REDACTED' \n  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \n  -d '{"model":"redwood-embed-1b","input":[[...1536 floats...]]}'
```
Response: 400 {"error":"dimension mismatch: expected 1024, got 1536"}  (request_id=rid_0a9f2c)

marta: Customer says this started after they upgraded their client lib which now batch-concats vectors on their side. They suspect batching changed the shape. They attached a few logs — I pasted the relevant bits below.

marta: Server log for rid_0a9f2c:
```
E 2026-03-12T14:22:17.123Z embedding-service:validate_vector ShapeError: vector length 1536 != model_dim 1024 model=redwood-embed-1b tenant=corp_zephyr
```

alex: Adding context from support triage — customer code is doing np.reshape before sending. Looks like client used a prepack step meant for a different model. They were previously on redwood-embed-2k (which is 1536) and migrated config but not the preproc.

kevin: quick confirm from runtime side: redwood-embed-1b is fixed-output-dim 1024. Some older models we shipped (embed-2k-compat) were 1536 — that mismatch can easily slip in. The API validates vector length on ingestion/indexing and returns 400.

kevin: On batching: our endpoint accepts an array of input vectors (shape [n, d]) or a single string / text to embed. If client inadvertently flattens a batch into a 1D array, the server will interpret that as one vector and validate dimension. So typical symptoms: user intended shape (8,1536) but sent (12288,) — server sees 12288 vs expected 1024 -> dimension error.

marta: Customer claims they did send nested arrays. I asked for the raw JSON they POSTed; waiting. Meanwhile, what should the immediate support runbook steps be?

kevin: Runbook (quick triage) — copy/paste this: 
1) Ask for the exact request body (first 1-2 vectors ok).
2) Confirm model param in the request (model=...).
3) Confirm the model's expected dim (we keep table below).
4) If they send base64 or binary, ensure decoding yields expected float32 array length.
5) Check request_id in server logs and paste logs (we can correlate).
6) If they recently upgraded client lib, ask for version and whether they changed any prepack/pooling code.

kevin: Example Python repro that fails when shapes are wrong: 
```python
import requests, numpy as np
v = np.random.rand(8,1536).astype('float32')
# OOPS: flattens accidentally
body = {"model":"redwood-embed-1b","input": v.flatten().tolist()}
r = requests.post(url, json=body, headers=headers)
print(r.status_code, r.text)
```
Fix is send v.tolist() (list of vectors), not v.flatten().tolist().

marta: Good. I'll send that to the customer. Also they asked about batching throughput — they're trying to push 2k reqs/s with 512-vector batches and seeing CPU throttles. Any throughput guidance?

kevin: For embedding throughput: use batch sizes tuned to model memory/latency. For redwood-embed-1b on our default host, sweet spot is batch 64–128 for best GPU utilization. Larger batches increase throughput but also increase tail latency. If they're using CPU fallback in Dedicated/Private, throughput will be far lower. Also make sure they enable continuous KV cache? (not relevant for embedding but just checking)

marta: Customer is on Hosted. They reported spikes in 5xx rates when they tried giant batched payloads; request_id for a 5xx example is rid_0a9f7e. Could be timeouts upstream.

kevin: For 5xx on huge payloads, we have an ingress size limit and memory guardrails that can OOM early. Recommend they chunk into smaller batches. We should also instrument a clearer error: currently returns 500 with opaque message when request payload > 64MB — I'll file an infra issue.

sophie: Docs/FAQ notes: I can add a dedicated FAQ: 'Embeddings dimension mismatch & batching pitfalls' and a short runbook. Suggested bullets:
- Table of model -> output dimension (redwood-embed-1b: 1024, embed-2k-compat:1536, tiny-embed:256)
- Example fixes: don't flatten, ensure shape [n, d], dtype float32 when sending raw arrays, or use SDK helpers that validate shape.
- Best-practice for throughput: recommended batch sizes per model and max payload guidance (e.g., keep request body < 16MB for fast path).

sophie: I'll draft a PR for the FAQ and include the code snippets above. Will also add a link from the embeddings API reference. ETA end of day tomorrow. :+1:

marta: Customer sent their exact JSON — they actually did send a nested array. But they set header "X-Client-Embedding-Dim: 1536" which our service ignores; we rely on model param and vector length. They thought the header controlled dynamic resizing.

kevin: We don't use that header anywhere. Good catch. Can you ask them to remove that header and re-send matching vectors to model dim? But also: maybe we should log a warning if we see a user-supplied dimension header mismatch — less confusing.

marta: Will do. Also raising this as a docs gap: 'headers won't override model dims' — Sophie will add that.

alex: For support handoff: If customer confirms their client is correct and they're still getting 400 with valid shapes, escalate to eng-ml with: request_id, raw request body (first 10 vectors redacted if sensitive), tenant id, and time window. We should toggle debug-run on their tenant to capture wire payloads.

infra-bot: deployment-notice: embeddings-service v1.12 deployed to prod at 2026-03-11T03:10Z (commit abc123) — no schema-change.

marta: Customer applied the fix (reshaped client) and re-tested — success, vectors accepted, indexing proceeded. They still want stronger docs and better errors for oversized payloads.

sophie: PR opened: docs#1482 'embeddings-batching-dimension-mismatch' — will include table + quick triage.

kevin: I'll open infra ticket to make payload-too-large return a clearer 413 with suggestion to chunk batches and include our model dimension table link.

marta: Closing loop with customer. Leaving thread for docs/infra to follow up. Thanks all. :rocket:
